turns.user: how do I do a deadlift
turns.reply:
1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart, mid-foot directly under the bar.
2. Hinge at your hips to reach down, grip the bar just outside your legs, and pull your chest up so your back is flat.
3. Drive through your feet to stand straight up, keeping the bar close to your shins the whole way.

Doing Romanian deadlifts today will practice that exact hip-hinge pattern for your lower body session.

turns.reply:
Here is the complete breakdown for setting up and pulling safely:

1. Setup — Stance and Grip
Place your feet hip-width apart with the bar over your mid-foot. Bend at the hips to take an overhand grip just outside your knees.

2. Positioning — Wedge and Tension
Pull your shins forward until they touch the bar. Lift your chest and squeeze your armpits back to engage your lats, taking the slack out of the bar before you lift.

3. The Pull — Leg Press the Floor
Take a deep breath into your belly and brace. Drive your feet into the floor to start the bar moving upward, keeping it in contact with your shins and thighs.

4. Lockout — Stand Tall
Squeeze your glutes to finish standing straight up. Avoid leaning backward or pulling with your lower back at the top.

5. Lowering — Control the Hinge
Push your hips back first to let the bar slide down your thighs. Once it clears your knees, bend your legs to touch the plates back to the floor.

Your Romanian deadlifts today use this exact top-half pattern, which builds the control needed for pulling off the floor.
